subject: SDK prefetch tunable & trace-id propagation — FinEdge field repro
messages:
From: Ravi Shah <ravi.shah@finedge.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Anya Ivanova <anya@finedge.ai>
Date: 2027-04-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: urgent: prefetch stalls + runtime errors in scale test

Hi Tessa —

Thanks for taking this quickly. We started a scale run overnight and saw repeated request failures that appear correlated with prefetch being enabled in the SDK. Symptoms:

- A subset of requests get a 500-level runtime error with message: "kvcache-invalidation: key mismatch during prefetch"
- Failures are intermittent (approx 0.5% of requests) but spike when concurrent in-flight requests exceed ~180
- When we disable prefetch the failures stop, but latency increases ~20% and cost goes up

Attached: fineedge-error-log.txt (server stack traces) and a tiny repro script (finedge-repro.sh) that reliably flips an in-flight request to the bad path after 1–2 minutes of steady traffic.

We need:
- A short-term mitigation we can apply without complete removal of prefetch (we rely on it for cost)
- An internal reproduction and a plan/ETA for a fix or a safe opt-out knob in the SDK/runtime

Cc'ing Anya (Eng) — she can share more console logs if helpful.

Thanks,
Ravi
Ravi Shah
Head of Platform Engineering, FinEdge

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Shah <ravi.shah@finedge.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-26T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: urgent: prefetch stalls + runtime errors in scale test

Hi Ravi —

Appreciate the logs and repro. Looping in Karthis and Dev from Platform/Runtime so we can triage. Initial notes:

- Thanks for the repro script — that's super useful.
- Short-term options we can consider today: a) expose an SDK-level prefetch throttle (lower concurrency threshold) b) opt-out flag per-route to disable prefetch for certain prompts, c) run your workload on a dedicated pool while we debug.

Ask for you / Anya: can you confirm the SDK version and whether you have persistent keepalive connections (yes/no)? Also share whether this occurs more often for long system prompts (we've seen K/V cache alignment issues there).

Planned next steps (tentative):
- Karthis/Dev: attempt to repro on a dedicated test cluster using the script Ravi provided
- If repro matches, create a minimal server-side patch to tighten KV cache validation and add a debug trace-id per request so we can correlate traces
- I'll coordinate a short working session tomorrow 9am PT to run the script together and collect logs

I'll also create a HubSpot note and link a Jira SUP.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Ravi Shah <ravi.shah@finedge.ai>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-26T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDK prefetch tunable & trace-id propagation — FinEdge field repro

Thanks for the signal -- digging in. A few clarifying items before we spin up a repro cluster:

1) SDK version: we need the exact client version string (e.g. 2.3.1+commit) and the language (node/python). Different code paths exist for JS vs. Python prefetch.
2) Persistent connections: confirm whether keepalive/pooling is enabled and the pool size.
3) Example of the prompt length and any non-UTF tokens (we've seen edge cases with unusual tokenizers)

On our side I will:
- Create a feature-flag branch that exposes two knobs to customers behind an opt-in: (A) prefetch_concurrency_limit, (B) prefetch_prefetch_window_ms. These are quick to surface in the SDK and should let you trade latency for stability.
- Add per-request trace-id propagation into the runtime logs (to correlate the SDK request -> server-side cache operations). This is low-risk and we'll put it on an internal build for you to run.
- If the repro matches, we will open SUP-4378 and attach artifacts.

Temporary mitigation suggestion: set prefetch_concurrency_limit=32 and prefetch_prefetch_window_ms=150 (instead of defaults) and run for 2 hours. Can one of you change that flag in your client and report results?

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Platform/Runtime, Redwood Inference

From: Ravi Shah <ravi.shah@finedge.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Anya Ivanova <anya@finedge.ai>
Date: 2027-04-27T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDK prefetch tunable & trace-id propagation — FinEdge field repro

Thanks Karthik — quick answers:

- SDK: node 2.3.1 (package.json shows 2.3.1)
- Keepalive: yes, we use persistent connections with pool size 100
- Prompt: primary repro uses a long system prompt ~4.8k chars (mostly plain English), and a short user prompt. No exotic tokens but the system prompt does contain a few unicode currency characters.

I've attached the repro script (finedge-repro.sh) and a trimmed server log segment. We toggled prefetch_concurrency_limit to 32 per your suggestion and ran for 3 hours — failure rate dropped but did not fully disappear (from 0.5% to 0.08%). With prefetch off the failures drop to near zero.

Happy to join the 9am PT session tomorrow.

-Ravi

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Ravi Shah <ravi.shah@finedge.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-28T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDK prefetch tunable & trace-id propagation — FinEdge field repro

Folks —

Quick summary from the internal triage run we did with Ravi's script:

- We reproduced the KV cache mismatch within our internal test cluster when pool size is large and multiple concurrent prefetches overlap for the same session id. Root cause appears to be a race during prefetch window eviction where two prefetch workers can update the same cache key without ordering guarantees.
- Short-term plan (this week):
  * Ship a server-side guard that serializes prefetch cache writes for the same session id (low-risk patch) — target: 72 hours to rollout to canary.
  * Expose the prefetch_concurrency_limit and prefetch_prefetch_window_ms as customer-configurable knobs in the SDK and Console — ETA: config toggle in 48 hours, UI/Console follow-up next week.
  * Add per-request trace-id propagation to logs so FinEdge and our team can correlate failed requests — internal build available after today's CI run.

Action items for Sales/CS:
- Tessa/Marissa: coordinate with FinEdge to enable the opt-in canary after we deploy the guard to canary (we will provide the build & instructions).
- Offer FinEdge a short-term escape hatch (priority routing to a dedicated pool) while canary runs; Gordon in Sales Ops suggested a one-week credit for extra runtime if they move to dedicated capacity during the investigation.

I'll attach the SUP ticket once it's created. Thanks all for rapid responses — we'll keep updates in SUP-4378 and the HubSpot deal.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
